finding: Modified Test 5 asserts `--record` "computes it not-clean for such a wholly severity-less round" where the round is defined only as "a new round that has at least one finding where no finding carries a severity (every finding omitted it)" — with no survival qualifier. But §3.4 states the not-clean rule "applies only to a *wholly* severity-less round ... yet at least one finding survives," and evaluates the zero-surviving case first: a round where every finding is resolved wontfix/duplicate has zero survivors and is clean under both `blocking` and `all`. So a wholly severity-less round whose only finding is resolved wontfix is clean per §3.4 but not-clean per Test 5. A test writer cannot deterministically decide the resolved-severity-less case; two engineers would write contradictory assertions.
suggestion: Add the surviving qualifier to Test 5 to match §3.4: assert `--record` computes not-clean only for a wholly severity-less round with at least one surviving (unresolved) finding, and add a companion case asserting a wholly severity-less round with every finding resolved wontfix/duplicate is clean (zero-surviving-first).

finding: Test 5 (modified this round) says `--record` "persists that flag and computes it not-clean for such a wholly severity-less round" with no "at least one finding survives" qualifier — but §3.4 restricts the severity-less not-clean rule to a round where "no finding carries a severity at all, yet at least one finding survives," evaluating the zero-surviving case FIRST (clean under both settings). A new round this release whose findings are all severity-less AND all resolved `wontfix`/`duplicate` (zero surviving), or an empty round, is simultaneously "zero surviving" (clean per §3.2/§3.4 and Test 20) and "wholly severity-less" per Test 5's literal wording (not-clean). Test 5 thus contradicts Test 20 and §3.4's zero-surviving-first ordering, giving the implementer two conflicting acceptance assertions for the same input.
suggestion: Add the survival guard to Test 5 to match §3.4: `--record` computes not-clean only for a wholly severity-less round with at least one *surviving* finding; a wholly severity-less round with zero surviving findings (all resolved wontfix/duplicate, or empty) is clean under the zero-surviving-first rule (§3.2, Test 20). Rephrase to e.g. "...computes it not-clean for such a wholly severity-less round that still has a surviving finding."
